literal: Zeal possession is the true possession; material wealth possession, without staying, departing will go away.
translation: The possession of inner motivation is the only true possession; the possession of material wealth does not last, but will slip away.
modern: ஊக்கத்தை உடைமையாகக் கொண்டிருப்பதே நிலையான உடைமையாகும்; பொருள் உடைமையாக இருப்பது நிலைத்து நிற்காமல் நம்மை விட்டு நீங்கிவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts internal strength with external riches. The word 'uḷḷam' here refers to the inner energy, zeal, or motivation of a person. The poet asserts that having this inner drive is the only permanent and real possession ('uṭaimai') one can own. On the other hand, material wealth ('poruḷ') is transient; it lacks stability and will eventually depart ('nīṅki viṭum') from a person. Therefore, cultivating a motivated mind is far more valuable than gathering material goods.
